Timestamps are from YouTube auto-captions (word-level) except Arirang and KDKA, whose captions are broadcast closed captions (sentence-level, about plus or minus 1 s). Shai-Hulud, xz-utils, F5, Salesloft and Salt Typhoon produced no broadcaster clips with usable lines; Log4j and NotPetya coverage did.

aiClips.aiLine: The supply chain attacks the Liamworm is leveraging are complex and deep rooted in software all computers on earth depend on. One expert I spoke to said by the time we figure one out seven new ones have popped up. And we just can't understand them fast enough to fix them all.

candidates.name: 06-cbsn-log4j-baked-in-variations
candidates.event: Log4j (Log4Shell) vulnerability, December 2021; CBSN tech reporter Dan Patterson with anchor Elise Preston
candidates.speaker: expert on camera (tech reporter on webcam, remote, home bookshelf behind him)
candidates.quote: it could be next to impossible because that vulnerability is so deeply baked into the software that they use every day
candidates.onScreenText: SOFTWARE FLAW THREATENS MILLIONS OF USERS GLOBALLY / VULNERABILITY COULD ALLOW BAD ACTORS TO ACCESS DEVICES, DATA AND HOLD SYSTEMS FOR RANSOM; small promo bug NOW: KIM POTTER TRIAL COVERAGE cbsnews.com/minnesota; LIVE CBSN
candidates.picture: Patterson full-frame on a webcam feed (grey suit, glasses, earbud), CBSN red lower third. At 187-200 s a chart ATTEMPTS TO EXPLOIT LOG4J VULNERABILITY SINCE DISCOVERY ON DECEMBER 9TH (40K to 830K in 72 h) fills the right two thirds with Patterson in a box on the left. At 78-100 s he is boxed beside server-room B-roll.
candidates.editPlan: Sound and picture both from Patterson. Fragment B 241.6-249.5 'it could be next to impossible because that vulnerability is so deeply baked into the software that they use every day' then fragment C 187.3-200.0 'within 72 hours of its discovery there were over 45 different variations, a little while later that increased to 60 variations' (chart on screen, the AI clip's graphic beat). About 20 s; trim C to 190.5-200.0 for 17 s, or use B alone (8 s) if the montage needs it short. Alternative longer bed, same speaker, 78.5-100.0: 'a number of cyber security experts have compared this to salt that is mixed into the batter, and once victims identify where this vulnerability is it is hard to extract it because as they say it's already been baked into the software tools they use'. Drop every mention of Log4j by name (not in these windows). The anchor's intro 20.96-34.2 'the discovery of a technical flaw in a popular open source software used by companies and consumers around the globe, the vulnerability could impact some of the most commonly used devices in our everyday life' is voice-over on laptop B-roll, usable as a bed but not an anchor on camera.
candidates.caveats: Webcam picture, not a desk anchor; 2021 pandemic remote look. Chart titles carry DECEMBER 9TH and DEC. 11/12/13 in medium type, legible at 480p; crop the top of the chart or accept. The KIM POTTER TRIAL bug dates it for anyone who remembers. Says 'vulnerability' and 'variations', never 'supply chain' or 'worm'.

candidates.name: 06-cnbc-javers-log4j-embedded-patches
candidates.event: Log4j vulnerability, first trading day after disclosure; Eamon Javers report from CNBC Washington
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk (correspondent on camera in studio, with side graphic)
candidates.quote: now the challenge here is that this software is embedded in so many products it means just about every company will be impacted by this new flaw which is just coming to light and since there are so many vendors involved here it's not clear at all when all of these patches will be made and that means the bad guys will have an open door for a long time to come
candidates.onScreenText: NEW CYBER FLAW POSES RISK TO THOUSANDS OF PRODUCTS; LOG4J EMBEDDED IN MANY PRODUCTS, POSES CHALLENGES; CISA WORKING WITH PUBLIC & PRIVATE SECTOR ON LOG4J; CISA: LOG4J 'URGENT CHALLENGE' GIVEN BROAD USE; side panel WHAT IS LOG4J? Popular java open source library for logging data / Used in everything from Apple's iCloud to the Mars Rover; CISA STATEMENT full-screen card at ~92 s dated December 11
candidates.picture: Javers on camera, dark suit, blue CNBC studio wall, THE EXCHANGE lower third; the WHAT IS LOG4J? panel sits on the right from ~40 s. Closest match to the AI clip's anchor-with-graphic look.
candidates.editPlan: Keep 92.9-99.4 'now the challenge here is that this software is embedded in so many products, it means just about every company will be impacted by this new flaw', cut 99.4-101.6 ('which is just coming to light and'), keep 101.6-111.2 'since there are so many vendors involved here it's not clear at all when all of these patches will be made and that means the bad guys will have an open door for a long time to come'. About 16 s. Start after the CISA statement card has left (it is on screen at 92-93 s; start at 93.2 if needed). Alternative 35.0-54.3: 'the software here is so ubiquitous, it's a popular java open source library for logging data and it's embedded in thousands of products, [Alperovitch] says it's used in everything from Apple's iCloud to the Mars rover and there's no guarantee that software publishers will be able to patch the problem before hackers take advantage of it' (drop 'alprovich says' 44.2-46.2).
candidates.caveats: Chyrons name LOG4J in large type, legible at 480p; fine for this audience but it fixes the incident to Dec 2021. The CISA statement card carries the date December 11 in small type. No 'worm' and no 'seven new ones', but 'not clear when all of these patches will be made' carries the same idea.

candidates.name: 06-cbsmornings-greenberg-cant-patch-spreads

candidates.speaker: expert on camera (guest at the anchor desk, single and two-shot)
candidates.quote: a piece of malware using zero-day vulnerabilities, vulnerabilities we haven't patched in our systems that we maybe can't patch, so it spreads unintentionally to the rest of the world
candidates.onScreenText: ANDY GREENBERG / WIRED SENIOR WRITER (to ~104 s), then $10 BILLION ATTACK / LESSONS TO BE LEARNED FROM DEVASTATING CYBERATTACK; at 128-131 s a full-screen card NOTPETYA CYBERATTACK, HACKING TOOLS USED: EternalBlue (created by the NSA, exploits Microsoft Windows system vulnerability) / Mimikatz (pulls passwords out of computers' memory, allows for multi-machine hacks)
candidates.picture: Greenberg (bald, red beard, dark jacket) in front of the CBS eye, then a two-shot with Thompson, then a wide of the whole desk at ~135 s.
candidates.editPlan: Start at 99.9, after 'this was Russian military intelligence hackers unleashing' (97.6-99.9), run to 112.7. Single speaker, one cut. For a 'worm' beat add 128.8-135.3 'then we need to be prepared to kind of recover quickly from these massive worms spread around the world' (the NotPetya card is on screen for the first half of it).
candidates.caveats: Describes an attack that already happened (past tense) rather than one unfolding; no 'deep-rooted in software everyone depends on'. 'Russian' must stay out. 2018 CBS This Morning set. The NotPetya card names EternalBlue and Mimikatz, a nice wink for this audience but it ties the clip to 2017.

candidates.name: 06-cnbc-easterly-log4j-vendors-of-vendors
candidates.event: CISA director Jen Easterly's first on-camera remarks on Log4j, Eamon Javers package
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk (Javers on camera) with CISA director on camera at 20.6-35 and 68.6-95.2
candidates.quote: because this is coming in from vendors and vendors of vendors and vendors of vendors of vendors so there's a lot of complicated steps that need to be done now
candidates.picture: not checked; by the audio it is Javers to camera with Easterly sound bites cut in
candidates.editPlan: Javers 120.7-129.0 as above, then 138.0-147.4 'it's this common little piece of software that software programmers just cut and paste and add it to other kind of products and it goes everywhere, it's just ubiquitous and that's the problem'. Easterly herself at 20.6-30.9: 'the log4j vulnerability is the most serious vulnerability that I have seen in my decades long career, everyone should assume that they are exposed and vulnerable' (needs 'log4j' muted or cut at 22.0). Also 86.4-95.2 Easterly: 'this is incredibly dangerous to everybody's business, everybody's networks, everybody's system'.
candidates.caveats: Not downloaded, so speaker and chyron unconfirmed. Easterly is recognisable to this audience, which is a plus or a date giveaway depending on taste. 'vendors of vendors of vendors' is the supply-chain idea without the words.

candidates.name: 08-cbs-uk-plc-hijacked-offline
candidates.publisher: CBS News (CBS Morning News / CBS News 24/7)
candidates.event: Telegraph report that Iran-linked hackers took a small UK power plant offline for four days (July 2026); Ramy Inocencio live from London
candidates.speaker: field reporter (foreign correspondent in a London box beside B-roll)
candidates.quote: the target was a computer in this power plant called programmable logic controller. Basically, you can think of it as a brain that ultimately looks out for power failures. If that happens, then it switches to a backup generator. Now, what appears to have happened was that this brain was hijacked and was offline for 4 days.
candidates.onScreenText: TELEGRAPH: IRAN-LINKED HACKERS TEMPORARILY SHUT DOWN A POWER PLANT IN THE UK; red bug WAR WITH IRAN; LONDON 12:19PM; CBS MORNING NEWS
candidates.picture: Inocencio in a small left-hand box (blue suit, striped tie, CBS News London globe backdrop); right two thirds is stock B-roll of a hooded figure at monitors, then green-lit keyboard, then a Tehran mural (from ~59 s). Not a plant.
candidates.editPlan: Sound: 40.3-46.7 'the target was a computer in this power plant called programmable logic controller' then 53.2-57.5 'what appears to have happened was that this brain was hijacked and was offline', optional tail 'for 4 days' to 58.4. About 10 s, one join at a sentence boundary, same voice. Picture: either keep Inocencio and crop or re-cover the lower third, or lay this sound under 08-france24-zaporizhzhia-cooling-towers-picture.
candidates.caveats: Lower third says IRAN-LINKED and UK in large type and the WAR WITH IRAN bug is on every frame; the fiction has no Iran, so crop the bottom 20 percent or replace it. Says 'power plant' and 'programmable logic controller', not nuclear or cooling valve; for a security audience PLC is better than microcontroller. 'hijacked' implies a human attacker.
